phrases: In eighteen fifty eight, the Thames smelled so bad
that Parliament hung curtains soaked in chemicals.
The river was full of raw sewage, in a very hot summer.
Disraeli called it a stygian pool, reeking with intolerable horrors.
Parliament quickly passed a bill for new sewers.
Engineer Joseph Bazalgette built about eighty miles of them.
Part of that system still serves London today.
It took a terrible smell to make politicians act.
Would you have stayed in the room?
